Home Effect Types Fuzz ToneBender variants Supa Tone Supa Tone Grinding distortion for guitar or bass Based on the 1974 "Supa Tonebender" fuzz by Colorsound™ The Colorsound Supa Tonebender was not based on a germanium Tone Bender design but is actually a variant of the Big Muff™ circuit, involving the deletion of the first set of clipping diodes. This has the effect of making it sound bassier and rougher than the streamlined compression of the original Big Muff design; this also makes it an ideal bass fuzz and sounds remarkably like a Marshall 2204 on guitar. read more reviews clips SKU: Supa-deposit MPN: SKR-SUPA Stock Status: Preorder Delivery Status: Lead time of about 2 weeks We build everything to order. Our current wait time is approximately 2 weeks to 1 month. I will confirm your order shortly, and I will send you a PayPal invoice for the total amount due including shipping when your order is ready. --Marc Price: $259 + shipping Mids switch voicing (see description below) Guitar Bass $259 $233.10 (10% off) 50% deposit $116.55 Quantity qty Add To Cart Reviews • Clips • Manual Available with 2 different voicings of the mids toggle switch: Guitar , with classic 1974 mids scoop to the left and flat mids to the right Bass , where the Mids switch has been changed to a "Guitar/Bass" switch.  Guitar mode (left) is a classic scooped sound like the original circa 1974 fuzz, and Bass mode (right) preserves ALL of the brutal bass throughout the tone knob's sweep. Illustrated here is the bass version... The guitar-voiced version will not have the mini toggle switch labeled, but that will operate between scooped and flat mids. Bass Voicing: When mids switch is set to "bass," grindy, tubey distortion that stays in the pocket You get a fuzzed attack but it's still punchy and retains the normal decay envelope All the low end is preserved in Bass mode, so the tone knob becomes a treble knob and does not thin out the tone even at full clockwise. Mids switch set to "guitar" is the classic 1974 scooped tone stack Guitar Voicing: Rough, unrefined, grinding, low-gain fuzz More raw & dynamic, less compressed and sustainy than a Big Muff* Low sustain-knob setting makes a nice cranked JCM900* emulation Mids switch selects between scooped and flat mids *Note: we have no affiliation with Colorsound or Electro-Harmonix or Marshall, who of course own their trademarked names. Skreddy Pedals browse by type distortion/fuzz/overdrive fuzz browse by enclosure pedal Skreddy Pedals Supa Tone Published on June 12, 2010 Skreddy Pedals fuzz pedal Information Skreddy Pedals Skreddy Pedals™ Supa Tone: based on a 1974 edition of a fuzz released by Colorsound™, this circuit is not based on a germanium Tone Bender design but is a variant of the Big Muff™ circuit. The first pair clipping diodes is removed, so there is more clean boost in front of the remaining pair of clipping diodes. Like the originals, I've used all polyester film coupling capacitors to retain every bit of high end rasp. I've used low-gain transistors (also like the originals) to retain dynamics and avoid going into syrupy-sustain territory. The tone stack is the original mid scoop, with my customary flat-mids switch added in case you have need of it.
